journey.name: Loopky as a signer — approving another app's sign-in from Settings → Sessions
journey.description:
An account whose key Loopky holds (created or restored in the app, journeys 20/22) approves another app's pubkyauth://signin_grant request itself, as Pubky Ring does, and lists and revokes the apps it approved (Architecture.md §7.10). Android also answers the link by deeplink, through an activity-alias enabled only while a key is held; iOS is scan and paste only.
Needs a staging account with a local key (see the local-key test accounts) and, for the Ring steps, a second install signed in with Pubky Ring. The CLI step needs `loopky` built from this branch (`./gradlew :cli:installDist`).

actions.action: Signed in with a held key, open Settings and verify "settings_sessions" sits under "settings_back_up_account". Tap it and verify "sessions_scan", "sessions_paste", and one row marked "This device" with no Revoke

CLI. On a computer run `loopky login --env staging --url-only --timeout 300`. Copy the printed link to the phone's clipboard and tap "sessions_paste". Verify "approval_sheet" says an app calling itself "loopky.app" wants to sign in, asks for "Read and write your Loopky decks", and shows "Approve only if you started this sign-in yourself"
Tap "approval_approve" and verify "approval_done_body". On the computer verify `loopky login` exits 0 and `loopky whoami --json` names the same pubky as Settings
Tap "approval_done" and verify the list now has a second row, with "session_revoke_0"

PUBKY.APP. pubky.app's own "Continue with Pubky Ring" button on a phone is an intent bound to Ring's package and goes to the Play Store, never Loopky; its DESKTOP sign-in shows a plain signin_grant QR. Scan that with "sessions_scan" (on an emulator, read the link from Chrome's DevTools port and deliver it by intent). Verify the sheet's warning is the accent "reaches beyond your Loopky decks" line and the access reads "Read and write /pub/pubky.app/". Approve and verify pubky.app signs in as the same account

SEARCH. Paste a fresh signin_grant link into Discover's search and verify "search_sign_in_link" offers "search_approve_sign_in" ("Approve in Loopky"), not "search_get_ring". Tap it and verify Sessions opens with the approval sheet for that link. On an install signed in with Ring, verify the row offers "search_get_ring" instead. On iOS this is the reliable paste path: the system Paste button in Sessions stays dimmed until the pasteboard holds text, and the Mac's pasteboard reaches the simulator only through the Simulator window

ANDROID DEEPLINK. With a key held, `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d '<a fresh signin_grant link>'` and verify Loopky opens on Sessions with the sheet up. Back out, reopen Loopky from recents, and verify the sheet does NOT come back

REVOKE. Tap "session_revoke_0", confirm "sessions_revoke_confirm", and verify the row leaves. On the computer verify the next write, e.g. `loopky deck create --env staging …`, exits 4 (session_expired); reads need no session

REFUSED. Paste a link whose caps are "/:rw", then one with "/pub/:rw", then a legacy "pubkyauth:///?caps=…" link and a signup_grant link. Verify each opens "approval_refusal" with its own reason and no Approve button
SECOND LINK. With a sheet in review, deliver a second link (paste or deeplink) and verify the sheet still shows the first request

RING USER. On an install signed in with Pubky Ring, verify Settings has no "settings_sessions", and on Android that tapping a signin_grant link opens Ring (or the system's no-handler message), never Loopky
SIGNED OUT. Sign the key account out and verify, on Android, that a signin_grant link no longer offers Loopky
TABLET and DARK. Verify the Sessions list and the sheet are width-capped and legible in both themes
